topic.title: where they were somebody
topic.claim: You moved your parents to your city to look after them. They lost the only place where they were somebody.
topic.moment: Papa sits on your sofa in a city where no shopkeeper knows his name, waiting for you to come home.

turn.believed: Bringing them to your city is the loving, obvious way to care for them.
turn.actually: You added years of safety and subtracted the whole world where they mattered.

topic.because: Back home papa was the man people greeted, mummy had her lane and her people. In your city they're just your parents, dependent and nameless, waiting on your schedule.
topic.payoff: You gave them a safer life and a smaller one. In your city they're safe. Back home, they were someone.
topic.feeling: the guilt hidden inside a good decision
topic.villain: the arrangement where care and belonging live in two different cities
topic.behaviour: adult kids relocate ageing parents to their own city for convenience and safety
topic.mechanism: the move trades their standing and community for your proximity, so they gain safety and lose the place they mattered
topic.group: adults who moved parents to live near them
topic.send_to: a friend weighing whether to bring their parents to the city
topic.why_now: post-Diwali, when many families make the 'move them here' decision
